title: Does nail gain from memory maps, and how should a build or a run choose them?
body:
nail reads three kinds of file through memory maps today, all through libsail's `MmapSource`:

- `io::Records` maps the query and target inputs with `Framed::map`, behind `io::Fasta` and `io::P7Hmm`.
- `PrefilterDb` maps each split file of the mmseqs prefilter db and of every align db, since `41781f9`.

libsail puts maps behind its `mmap` cargo feature. Its `source::Source` trait has one method, `range(start, len) -> io::Result<Cow<[u8]>>`, with two implementations. `FileSource` reads the range with a positioned read and returns an owned buffer. `MmapSource` returns a slice of the map. `Framed<S: Source>` is generic over the two, with `Framed::open` for a `FileSource` and `Framed::map` for an `MmapSource`.

The measurements so far are mixed. Mapping helped the input indexing and decide and merge in progressive seeding. It also raised peak RSS from 4.8 GB to 7.4 GB on a 32 GB prefilter db, and seeding misc time from 0.23 s to 0.74 s (nail-844b46). At MGnify scale, about 2.456 billion records over about 500 GB, the prefilter db and the RSS figure would be far larger. Nobody has compared the two sources across nail on the same runs.

## Proposal

First, evaluate. Run nail with each file kind on `FileSource` and on `MmapSource`, at more than one input size, and record wall time per leaf of the `-s` tree and peak RSS.

Then gate the maps the way libsail does, with the `cfg` in one module. libsail already supplies the trait and both sources, so nail needs no trait of its own. A sketch:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "mmap")]
pub type InputSource = MmapSource;
#[cfg(not(feature = "mmap"))]
pub type InputSource = FileSource;

pub fn open_source(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<InputSource>;
pub fn open_framed(path: &Path, format: Format) -> anyhow::Result<Framed<InputSource>>;
```

`Records` and `PrefilterDb` then hold `InputSource` and call `Source::range`.

## Options

| option | what it is | cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. map always | today | no choice for a user short on memory |
| B. cargo feature | `mmap` on or off at build time, as in libsail | release binaries carry one setting, which the release CI picks |
| C. runtime flag | a CLI param picks the source per run | both paths compiled into every binary, and a new CLI param |
| D. never map | `FileSource` everywhere | gives up the measured gains in indexing, decide and merge |

The lean is to settle the evaluation first. nail ships as a binary, so B fixes the choice per release build. C reaches users of the release binaries, and B reaches only users who build from source. The evaluation should say whether either source wins outright, which would make the choice moot.

## Open

- `PrefilterDb::next_n` scans a record for n newlines from its checkpoint. With a map that is a slice. With `FileSource` it needs reads in chunks, since a `range` call over the rest of a record can read megabytes for one query.
- `PrefilterDb::get` would return `Cow<[u8]>` under both sources, which changes its callers in `seed_stage.rs`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Measurements from nail-844b46, for this decision. On the 32 GB prefilter db of the full run (20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 mgy targets), slicing through the map grows the process's `RssFile` while `RssAnon` stays at 1 MB. A probe that keeps every query active reaches 31.6 GB of `RssFile` after 11 iterations. A real run reads less, because decide terminates queries; the full run peaked at 7.4 GB, against 4.8 GB before `41781f9`. The pages are clean file pages the kernel can drop. Peak RSS counts them, and `read` did not. Whether a cluster scheduler that enforces RSS limits counts mapped file pages has not been checked. The probe and its table are in the note on nail-844b46.

One option for `PrefilterDb` alone: `pread` from one `File` kept open per split file, into a reused buffer. That would bring RSS back to nail's own allocations. Its cost against the map for slice, decide and merge is not measured. Before `41781f9` those three leaves took 1.25 s together with a file reopened per record, and about 0.96 s with the map.

The null-byte check that made seeding `[misc.]` slow is gone in `c1cc1c0`, so the time cost no longer depends on this decision.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Compared both settings of a new cargo feature `mmap`, which picks `MmapSource` or `FileSource` for every input and every mmseqs db (uncommitted on `dev` after `c1cc1c0`). The search was 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 mgy targets, `--seed-mode prog`, `-t 8`, on the 16-core box. The mmap build ran first, then the file build. Both wrote 3,031,365 rows, identical once sorted. Script and logs are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-15-prefilter-map/full`.

| leaf | mmap | file |
|---|---|---|
| runtime | 698.23 s | 691.97 s |
| query index | 0.55 s | 0.40 s |
| target index | 0.44 s | 0.57 s |
| db write | 0.69 s | 0.71 s |
| prefilter | 179.58 s | 179.40 s |
| slice | 7.23 s | 0.71 s |
| align | 65.85 s | 65.74 s |
| decide | 0.10 s | 0.11 s |
| merge | 0.17 s | 0.18 s |
| seed index | 0.56 s | 0.54 s |
| alignment | 442.58 s | 443.16 s |
| peak RSS | 4.93 GB | 5.00 GB |

The only leaf apart by more than noise is slice. The mmap build's 7.23 s came with 9,906 major faults. The same leaf took 0.72 s with the map at `41781f9`, so it depends on how much of the 32 GB prefilter db is still in the page cache when slicing starts. The file build reads through `pread`, whose disk reads do not show as page faults, so the fault counts do not compare. The 7.4 GB peak RSS of `41781f9` did not recur with the map; the null-byte check that `c1cc1c0` removed probably accounted for part of it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Benchmark with reps: all 20,795 Pfam profiles against the first 1,000,000 mgy targets, `--seed-mode prog`, `-t 8`, on the 16-core box. There were 5 reps of each build in each cache state, after one warm-up run. The build order flipped every rep. Cold runs dropped both inputs' pages with `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`, and `fincore` confirmed 0 bytes resident before each run. Warm runs read both inputs first, and `fincore` confirmed them fully resident. The prefilter db was left as each run wrote it. All 20 runs wrote the same 1,296,370 rows. Scripts and logs are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-15-prefilter-map/bench1m`.

Means over 5 reps, in seconds:

| leaf | cold mmap | cold file | warm mmap | warm file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| runtime | 314.96 | 318.83 | 314.95 | 315.78 |
| runtime, median | 313.10 | 313.70 | 313.99 | 314.26 |
| query index | 0.59 | 0.68 | 0.39 | 0.46 |
| target index | 0.17 | 0.26 | 0.13 | 0.23 |
| slice | 0.35 | 0.34 | 0.36 | 0.34 |
| decide | 0.04 | 0.05 | 0.04 | 0.05 |
| merge | 0.04 | 0.10 | 0.04 | 0.10 |
| prefilter | 98.83 | 99.20 | 98.72 | 98.80 |
| align | 31.46 | 31.61 | 31.48 | 31.51 |
| alignment | 182.70 | 185.85 | 183.02 | 183.54 |
| peak RSS, GB | 6.97 | 2.59 | 6.97 | 2.59 |

The leaves that read through the source (query index, target index, decide, merge) are faster with the map by about 0.25 s in total. The runtime medians differ by 0.3 to 0.6 s, against a spread of 8 s between reps of one build. The cold file mean includes one run at 331.96 s. The alignment stage runs the same code in both builds, and it varied from 181 to 197 s across all runs. The map raised peak RSS by 4.4 GB.
